question: For a question about material flammability and fire spread (prevention): how much more important is it that an experiment matches the user's oxygen mole fraction (A) than the user's flow around the fuel (type and speed) (B)?
comment: A class 1 (C17, C15, C7); B class 1 (C7, C8, PSI-25). A: A solid burns only above a limiting oxygen concentration (the oxygen index; NASA's maximum oxygen concentration). In microgravity the flammability map in oxygen against flow has a low-oxygen limit. Oxygen can therefore decide whether a material burns at all. B: In microgravity, flow decides burning near the limits: flames quench at low flow (radiative loss) and blow off at high flow, with a flow of maximum flammability between. BASS-II names airflow speed and oxygen as its main variables.
